analysis:
Integration pass over the PR's visible changes: a changelog fragment; doc edits in hardware-support.md (line 97), inference.md (gpt_oss row, ~1163), prefix-cache.md (line 689) and configuration.md (lines 3 and 593); comment-only edits in EngineV2Bridge.swift (132-136), EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (201-204) and EngineV2KVSizing.swift (8-10); test updates in SegmentedProductionGrantTests.swift and SegmentedFleetGeometry.swift; and an opaque libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump (19634dd8 to 4aaf012c). No executable provider-swift code changes in the supplied evidence. Key custody, attestation, App Attest authorization, WebSocket handling and cache crypto are untouched.

T-041 (SSD prefix cache) is the relevant threat. The changelog says float32-layer GPT-OSS checkpoints land in a different namespace and are not restored, so stale ciphertext stays under the same HMAC names, AES-GCM and 30-minute TTL until it expires or the KEK is wiped. The at-rest exposure is unchanged in kind. The smaller per-token K/V (24,576 B vs 49,152 B) lowers disk and staging footprint.

The remaining question is availability and memory admission, loosely T-016/T-029. The 3.5 GiB activation floor is documented as unmeasured for bf16, and the fixtures and docs assume K/V halves. This is consistent with the claim that admission prices observed native per-layer types via EngineV2SlotFactory.slotKVBytesPerToken. That function is not supplied, so it could not be checked. The fallback in nativeKVBytesPerToken over-reserves, so it fails safe. The real behavior sits in the submodule bump, which I cannot inspect, so the dtype claim and the checkpoint-identity separation of bf16 vs fp32 caches (layoutEpoch/layer-type binding) are unverified. Those are unverified contracts, not demonstrated regressions.

A code-bearing pass should confirm that (1) the submodule's SwiGLU change yields bf16 K/V consistently with the paged pool dtypes, (2) admission and heartbeat kv_bytes_per_token use observed dtypes, and (3) the checkpoint namespace includes layer dtypes. It should also check coordinator-side agreement on the halved kv_bytes_per_token, since that policy is platform-owned. No findings.
